questions.question: ______ expenditure and ______ receipts are shown by the government budget.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Estimated; estimated.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **The government budget shows estimated expenditures and estimated receipts.**
 
• **Estimated expenditure and actual receipts** would mean that the government has budgeted a certain amount of spending but has actually received a different amount of revenue.
 
• **Actual expenditure and estimated receipts** would mean that the government has spent a certain amount but expects to receive a different amount of revenue.
 
• **Actual expenditure and actual receipts **would mean that the government has spent a certain amount and has received the exact amount of revenue that was expected.
 
• It is important for the government to accurately estimate its expenditures and receipts in order to create a realistic budget and avoid** **overspending or underspending.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Expenditure refers to the amount of money spent by the government on various expenses such as **salaries, infrastructure development, subsidies,** etc.
 
• Receipts refer to the amount of money collected by the government through various sources such as taxes, fines, fees, etc.
 
• **Estimated; actual** would indicate that the government's revenue collection strategy may be flawed or inefficient.
 
• **Actual; estimates** would indicate that the government's expenditure planning may be flawed or inefficient.
 
• **Actual; actual **would indicate that the government's budget planning and execution is accurate.

questions.question: What is the name of a metallic radioactive transuranic element with atomic number 101 in the actinide series, discovered in 1955?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Mendelevium.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The metallic radioactive transuranic element with atomic number 101 in the actinide series is called Mendelevium.**
 
• It was discovered in **1955** by a team of American scientists led by **Albert Ghiorso.**
 
• **Mendelevium is named after the Russian chemist Dmitri Mendeleev, who is known for creating the periodic table of elements.**
 
• It is a synthetic element, which means that it is not found naturally on Earth and can only be produced in a laboratory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Seaborgium** is a synthetic element with atomic number** 106.**

 
 
• It is named after the American chemist **Glenn T. Seaborg.**
 
 
 
• **Nobelium** is a synthetic element with atomic number **102.**
 
 
• It is named after **Alfred Nobel,** the inventor of dynamite.
 
 
 
• **Rutherfordium** is a synthetic element with atomic number **104.**
 
 
• It is named after the British physicist **Ernest Rutherford.**

questions.question: In which of the following Vedas was Dasarajna war (the war of ten kings) mentioned?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rigveda.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dasarajna war **(the war of ten kings) was mentioned in the **Rigveda.**
 
• This war was fought between the **Puru and Bharata tribes** and was one of the earliest recorded conflicts in ancient India.
 
• The Rigveda describes the **battle in detail, **including the names of the ten kings and the strategies they used.
 
• **The outcome of the war was in favor of the **Bharata **tribe, and their leader Sudas emerged victorious.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Rigveda** is the oldest and most important of the four Vedas in ancient Indian literature.

 
 
• **It offers a wealth of information about the beginnings of the world, the significance of the Gods, and practical tips for leading a happy and prosperous life.**
 
 
 
• The **Yajurveda **contains hymns and rituals related to **sacrificial ceremonies.**
 
 
• **​This text offers details about the Aryan people's social and religious lives.**
 
 
 
• The **Samaveda** focuses on melodies and chants** **used in religious ceremonies.
 
 
• **The Samaveda is divided into two sections: Part I consists of songs named Gana and Part II consists of a book of three poems called Archika.**
 
 
 
• The **Atharvaveda **contains** **spells and incantations for various purposes, including healing and protection.
 
 
• **The twenty Kandas that make up the Atharva Veda are further divided into thirty-six Prapathakas.**

questions.question: What is the percentage share of agricultural workers in India as per Census 2011?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**54.6%.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The percentage share of agricultural workers in India as per Census 2011 is 54.6%.**
 
• This means that out of the total workforce in India, only 54.6% were engaged in agricultural activities as per the 2011 Census.
 
• This is a significant drop from the previous Census in 2001, which recorded **60% **of the total workforce as agricultural workers.
 
• **The decline in the percentage share of agricultural workers in India can be attributed to various factors such as industrialization, urbanization, and the shift towards the service sector.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agricultural workers form a significant portion of the workforce in India, and the sector contributes to around** **17% of India's GDP.**
 
• The decline in the percentage share of agricultural workers in India has led to concerns about the sustainability of the agricultural sector and the livelihoods of farmers.
 
• Agriculture accounted for **43.96 percent** of India's workforce in **2021.**
 
• **The remaining half was split nearly evenly between the two other sectors, industries and services.**
 
• Even if the percentage of Indian workers in agriculture is decreasing, it remains the primary industry for employment.

questions.question: Who introduced the system of Dagh and Huliyah and cash payment to soldiers in the Delhi sultanate?

• This helped in maintaining a** strong army.**
 
• He also introduced the system of** **cash payment to soldiers, which was a departure from the earlier practice of granting land as payment.
 
• This helped in boosting the morale of the soldiers and ensuring their loyalty.
 
• **Alauddin Khalji was a powerful ruler of the Delhi Sultanate who ruled from 1296 to 1316.**
 
• **He was known for his military conquests and administrative reforms.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• He was known for his patronage of** **art and architecture, and for his construction of public works such as canals and hospitals.
 
 
 
• **Jalaluddin Khalji was the first ruler of the Khalji dynasty who ruled from 1290 to 1296.**
 
 
• He was known for his military campaigns and for his attempts to establish a stable administration.
 
 
 
• **Ghiyasuddin Tughluq was the founder of the Tughluq dynasty who ruled from 1320 to 1325.**
 
 
• He was known for his** **administrative** **reforms** **and for his attempts to centralize power in the Delhi Sultanate.

• This relationship is known as the Geiger-Nuttall law, which states that the logarithm of the half-life of an alpha decay is proportional to the reciprocal of the square root of the energy of the alpha particle.

questions.question: The length of the pitch in cricket is ______

The correct answer is __**22 yards.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **The correct length of the pitch in cricket is 22 yards or 20.12 meters.**
 
• This measurement is taken from the** bowling crease** to the batting crease.
 
• The length of the pitch has remained the same since the **19th century.**
 
• **The size of the pitch is important in cricket as it affects the gameplay and scoring opportunities.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The pitch is a rectangular area of the ground that is 22 yards long and 10 feet wide.**
 
• **The pitch is made up of different areas including the batting crease, bowling crease, and the popping crease.**
 
• Two teams of eleven players compete in the bat-and-ball game of cricket on a field in the middle of the pitch.
 
• Either team has a wicket at either end, which is made up of two bails balanced on three stumps.
 
• While the bowling and fielding side tries to stop this and **dismiss every batter**, the batting side earns runs by hitting the ball bowled at one of the wickets with the bat and then sprinting between the wickets.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Acromegaly - Adrenaline.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acromegaly is a hormonal disorder that results in the excessive production of growth hormone, which is produced by the pituitary gland.**
 
• Adrenaline is not associated with acromegaly.
 
• Instead, it is a hormone that is produced by the adrenal glands and is involved in the body's "fight or flight" response.
 
• **Cushing's syndrome is a condition that is caused by the overproduction of cortisol, a steroid hormone that is produced by the adrenal glands.**
 
• Diabetes is a condition that is characterized by high levels of glucose (sugar) in the blood.
 
 
• **It is caused by a lack of insulin, a hormone that is produced by the pancreas.**
 
 
 
• **Thyroxin**, which is associated with goitre, is involved in regulating **metabolism and growth**. 
 
 
• **It helps to regulate the body's energy production and influences the development of the brain, bones, and muscles.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cortisol,** which is associated with Cushing's syndrome, is involved in regulating a variety of bodily functions, including **metabolism, immune response, and stress response.**
 
• Insulin, which is associated with diabetes, regulates the levels of glucose (sugar) in the blood.
 
 
• **It allows cells to use glucose for energy and helps to store excess glucose in the liver and muscles.**
 
 
 
• Goitre is a condition that is characterized by an enlarged thyroid gland.
 
 
• **It is often caused by a deficiency of iodine, which is necessary for the production of thyroid hormones.**

questions.question: Who founded the independent State of Bengal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Murshid Quli Khan.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **The founder of the Independent State of Bengal was Murshid Quli Khan, who served as the governor of Bengal under the Mughal Empire from 1717 to 1727.**
 
• He managed to consolidate his power in the region and established an independent state with its capital at **Murshidabad.**
 
• Murshid Quli Khan was known for his **administrative and economic reforms, **which included introducing a new revenue system and promoting trade and commerce.
 
• His successors, including **Alivardi Khan and Siraj-ud-Daulah**, continued to rule the independent State of Bengal until it was annexed by the British East India Company in the mid-18th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alivardi Khan was the Nawab of Bengal from 1740 to 1756.**

 
 
• He was known for his military campaigns against the **Marathas and the Britis**h.
 
 
 
• **Sarafraz Khan was a governor of Bengal under the Mughal Empire in the early 18th century.**
 
 
• Sarfaraz Khan was **Murshid Khan's nominee** to succeed him as there was no direct successor.
 
 
 
• Shuja-ud-Din was a governor of Bengal under the Mughal Empire in the mid-18th century.
 
 
• He was** deposed by the British** before he could establish an independent state.

questions.question: Which of the following lines is NOT related to kabaddi?
questions.solution:
.The correct answer is __**Attack line**__

__
 
• The attack line is not a designated line or marking on the kabaddi court.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• **Baulk line: **The baulk line is at a distance of 3.75m from the midline.
 
• **Attack line: The attack line is an imaginary line that is approximately 3 meters away from the baulk line, on the opponent's side of the court.**
 
• When a raider crosses the attack line, they enter the bonus area and can earn extra points by touching or tagging opponents.
 
• **Bonus line: The bonus line is a small semicircular area located at the end of the opponent's half of the court. **
 
• When a raider enters the bonus area, they can earn extra points by touching or tagging opponents.
 
• **End line: The end line is a line drawn across the width of the court, marking the end of the playing area. **
 
• Players cannot cross the end line during the game.

Therefore, the attack line is not a physical line on the court, unlike the other options. It is a conceptual line that is used to define the bonus area and determine when a raider has entered or exited that area.
